references.text: The Passover lamb was to be slaughtered from the small livestock, either from the sheep or the goats, as part of the Passover celebration in Egypt.
Moses instructs the Israelites to slaughter the Passover lamb, which is the original Passover regulation.
The Passover offerings are described, including the specific animals that were to be sacrificed during the festival.
The place where the Lord would choose to have His name dwell is where the Israelites were to bring their offerings and worship.
The chosen place where the Lord lets His name dwell is where all offerings and gifts must be brought.
King Hezekiah celebrated Passover in Jerusalem, the place the Lord had chosen, with both small livestock and cattle.
King Josiah gave the people small livestock and cattle for the Passover sacrifices, in accordance with the regulation to offer both small livestock and cattle.
Those who returned from exile celebrated Passover and slaughtered the Passover lamb in Jerusalem, the place the Lord had chosen.
Jesus went up to Jerusalem to celebrate Passover, the place God had chosen for worship.
